simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-03.title: Substitute
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-03.body:
$ax-2by+3c=a(3a-4b^2)-2b(4b-3c^2)+3c=3a^2-4ab^2-8b^2+6bc^2+3c$.

This does not match options A to D (the value of $z$ is not needed).

**Answer: (E) None of the above**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-04.title: Evaluate the left side
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-04.body:
$1+2+\cdots+120=\frac{120\times121}{2}=7260$, so the left side is $\frac{7260}{110}=66$.

Then $2+4+6+N=132$, so $N=132-12=120$, which is not among options A to D.

**Answer: (E) None of the above**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-05.title: Use the common widths and heights
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-05.body:
Let the columns have widths $A,B,C$ and the rows have heights $D$ (top), $E$ (middle), $F$ (bottom). The given areas are $BD=1$, $AE=\frac16$, $CE=\frac12$, $AF=\frac13$, $BF=\frac23$.

From $AF=\frac13$ and $BF=\frac23$: $B=2A$. From $AE=\frac16$ and $CE=\frac12$: $C=3A$. From $AE=\frac16$ and $AF=\frac13$: $F=2E$.

Now the unknown areas: top-left $AD=\frac12BD=\frac12$ (since $A=\frac B2$), top-right $CD=\frac32BD=\frac32$, middle $BE=2AE=\frac13$, bottom-right $CF=3AF=1$.

Sum: $\frac12+\frac32+\frac13+1=\frac{10}{3}$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac{10}{3}$**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-06.title: Find $x$ first
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-06.body:
$8\,\triangle\,x=7\times6\times\cdots\times(8-x)=840$. Since $840=7\times6\times5\times4$, the last factor is $4=8-x$, so $x=4$.

Then $x\,\triangle\,(x-3)=4\,\triangle\,1=4-1=3$, which is not among A to D.

**Answer: (E) None of the above**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-08.title: Remove the roots and absolute values

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-09.title: Angles of the hexagon
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-09.body:
Draw $FX$ parallel to $HE$ and $DB$. Since $\angle H=138^\circ$, the angle between $FH$ and $FX$ is $180^\circ-138^\circ=42^\circ$, so $\angle DFX=90^\circ-42^\circ=48^\circ$ and then $\angle D=180^\circ-48^\circ=132^\circ$. Hence $\angle B=136^\circ$.

The hexagon $HEGBDF$ has angle sum $720^\circ$, with $\angle G=\angle F=90^\circ$:

$$\angle E=720^\circ-90^\circ-90^\circ-138^\circ-132^\circ-136^\circ=134^\circ.$$

**Answer: (A) $134^\circ$**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-10.title: Count numerators sharing a factor
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-10.body:
$2020=2^2\times5\times101$. A fraction is not in simplest form when its numerator is a multiple of $2$, $5$ or $101$.

Multiples of $2$: $100$; of $5$: $40$; of both ($10$): $20$. So $100+40-20=120$ numerators are multiples of $2$ or $5$. The only multiple of $101$ up to $200$ is $101$ itself, which is not a multiple of $2$ or $5$: one more.

Not in simplest form: $121$. In simplest form: $200-121=79$.

**Answer: (C) 79**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-11.title: Pair up the arrangements
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-11.body:
There are $5!=120$ arrangements of the digits. In exactly half of them the $2$ comes before the $4$: swapping the $2$ and the $4$ turns an arrangement with $2$ before $4$ into one with $4$ before $2$, and vice versa.

So Boris can write $\frac{120}{2}=60$ numbers.

**Answer: (C) 60**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-11.title: Choose positions
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-11.body:
Choose which $2$ of the $5$ positions hold the digits $2$ and $4$: $\binom52=10$ ways, and they must appear in the order $2$ then $4$. The three odd digits fill the other positions in $3!=6$ ways. Total $10\times6=60$.

**Answer: (C)**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-12.title: Compare triangles
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-12.body:
Let the distances from $A$, $M$, $B$ to line $DC$ be $h_a$, $h_m$, $h_b$. Since $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$, $h_m=\frac{h_a+h_b}{2}$.

Also $DN=NC=\frac12DC$. So

$$[ADN]+[BNC]=\tfrac12\cdot DN\cdot h_a+\tfrac12\cdot NC\cdot h_b=\tfrac14DC(h_a+h_b)=\tfrac12DC\cdot h_m=[DMC].$$

In terms of the parts: $[ADN]=S_1+S_3$, $[BNC]=S_6+S_7$ and $[DMC]=S_3+S_4+S_6$. Hence $S_1+S_3+S_6+S_7=S_3+S_4+S_6$, i.e. $S_1+S_7=S_4$.

**Answer: (B)**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-13.title: Powers of 2 modulo 7
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-13.body:
The remainders of $2^n$ on division by $7$ repeat with period $3$: $2,4,1,2,4,1,\ldots$ Since $2020=3\times673+1$, $2^{2020}$ leaves remainder $2$ when divided by $7$.

Two days after Tuesday is Thursday.

**Answer: (B) Thursday**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-14.title: Eliminate
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-14.body:
If Ellie and Audrey were at Westwood, the other three (Tom, Chris, Violet) would be at Greenwich, but Tom and Chris are at different schools. So Ellie and Audrey are at Greenwich, and exactly one of Tom, Chris and Violet is also there; the other two are at Westwood.

If Violet and Chris were in Secondary 3, then the other three, Audrey, Tom and Ellie, would all be Secondary 1, contradicting that Audrey and Tom are at different levels. So Violet and Chris are in Secondary 1.

The Secondary 3 student at Westwood is not Ellie or Audrey (Greenwich) nor Violet or Chris (Secondary 1). It is Tom.

**Answer: (D) Tom**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-15.title: Count trailing zeros
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-15.body:
The number of trailing zeros of $n!$ is $\lfloor n/5\rfloor+\lfloor n/25\rfloor+\lfloor n/125\rfloor+\cdots$. It increases by $1$ at multiples of $5$ that are not multiples of $25$, by $2$ at multiples of $25$ that are not multiples of $125$, and by $3$ at multiples of $125$.

The values that are skipped come from the jumps of $2$ or more: at $n=25$ the count jumps from $4$ to $6$ (skipping $5$); at $50$ from $10$ to $12$ (skip $11$); at $75$ from $16$ to $18$ (skip $17$); at $100$ from $22$ to $24$ (skip $23$); at $125$ from $28$ to $31$ (skip $29,30$); at $150$ from $35$ to $37$ (skip $36$); after $150$ the count reaches $40$ at $n=165$ with no further skips up to $40$.

Skipped values up to $40$: $5,11,17,23,29,30,36$, which is $7$ numbers.

**Answer: (C) 7**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-16.title: Read the chart in units
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-16.body:
Let each space of the chart be $x$ students. The bars for A, B, C, D, E and No response have $3x,7x,5x,8x,4x,4x$ students.

The $7x$ students who chose B score $14x$ points. The students who chose A, C, D or E number $3x+5x+8x+4x=20x$ and score $-20x$.

Total: $14x-20x=-6x=-240$, so $x=40$ and $7x=280$ students were correct.

**Answer: 280**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-17.title: Count in each block and add the crossing ones
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-17.body:
The figure is two $8\times8$ grids that touch along a common segment of length $4$ cells. Each grid contains $1^2+2^2+\cdots+8^2=204$ squares, so $408$ in total.

Now count the squares that use cells of both grids. Such a square must cross the common vertical line, and since the grids share only $4$ rows, its side is at most $4$. A square of side $k$ ($2\le k\le4$) crosses the line in $k-1$ horizontal positions and fits in $5-k$ vertical positions: $k=2$: $1\times3=3$; $k=3$: $2\times2=4$; $k=4$: $3\times1=3$. That makes $10$ more.

Total: $408+10=418$.

**Answer: 418**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-18.title: Chloe's walking time
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-18.body:
Let Chloe take $x$ minutes to reach the cinema, so the distance is $100x$ metres. By 12.10 p.m., $30$ minutes have passed. Chloe spent $x+10$ minutes before turning back, so she walked back for $30-x-10=20-x$ minutes, covering $100(20-x)$ metres.

Her cousin has walked $60\times30=1800$ metres from home. When they meet, the cousin's distance from home plus Chloe's distance from the cinema is the total distance:

$$1800+100(20-x)=100x\quad\Rightarrow\quad200x=3800,\ x=19.$$

Distance: $100\times19=1900$ metres.

**Answer: 1900 m**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-20.title: Divisible by 4 and 9
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-20.body:
Divisible by 4: $\overline{B4}$ must be divisible by 4, so $B$ is even; the only even prime is $B=2$.

Divisible by 9: the digit sum $7+A+3+4+2+4=20+A$ must be a multiple of $9$, so $A=7$ (giving $27$).

The number is $773424=36\times21484$.

**Answer: 7**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-21.title: Find the pattern
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-21.body:
The result is $2(a+b)$ followed by $3(b-a)$, written side by side: $4\wedge8$: $24$ and $12$; $2\wedge3$: $10$ and $3$.

So $7\wedge8$: $2(15)=30$ and $3(1)=3$, giving $303$.

**Answer: 303**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-22.title: Worst case
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-22.body:
So far $300+154+194+281+266+9=1204$ votes have been dealt with, so $1400-1204=196$ votes are still to be counted.

The main rival is D (281 votes). In the worst case all the votes that A does not get go to D. If A gets $t$ of the remaining $196$ votes, then A has $300+t$ and D has at most $281+196-t$. A wins for sure when $300+t>477-t$, i.e. $2t>177$, so $t\ge89$.

So A needs $300+89=389$ votes in total (with $388$, D could reach $389$).

**Answer: 389**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-23.title: Pythagoras with coordinates
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-23.body:
Let $AC=5x$ and $BC=5y$. Then $EC=2x$ and $DC=3y$.

In right triangle $BCE$: $(2x)^2+(5y)^2=10$, i.e. $4x^2+25y^2=10$. In right triangle $ACD$: $(5x)^2+(3y)^2=16$, i.e. $25x^2+9y^2=16$.

Solving: $x^2=\frac{10}{19}$, $y^2=\frac{6}{19}$. Then $AB^2=25(x^2+y^2)=25\times\frac{16}{19}=\frac{400}{19}$ and $57\times AB^2=57\times\frac{400}{19}=1200$.

**Answer: 1200**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-24.title: Set up equations
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-24.body:
Let $c$, $a$, $b$ be the numbers of roads $AB$, $BC$, $CA$. Going from A to C: $b+ca=33$. Going from B to C: $a+cb=23$.

Subtracting: $b-a+c(a-b)=10$, i.e. $(c-1)(a-b)=10$. With $3\le c\le10$, $c-1$ is $2$ or $5$ ($c=3$ or $6$).

- $c=3$, $a-b=5$: $b+3(b+5)=33$ gives $4b=18$, not an integer.
- $c=6$, $a-b=2$: $b+6(b+2)=33$ gives $b=3$, $a=5$. Check: $5+6\times3=23$. 

From B to A: directly $c=6$ ways, or via C in $a\times b=15$ ways: $6+15=21$.

**Answer: 21**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-25.title: Work from the left
simcc-sasmo-2020-g8-25.body:
In the ten-thousands column $S+(\text{carry})=M=6$ with $S\ne6$, so $S=5$ and a carry of $1$ arrives. For that carry, $A=9$ in the thousands column, and then $E=0$.

The remaining digits $W,I,O,D,L$ are $1,2,3,7,8$. The units column gives $4+O=L$ (mod 10) with $O,L$ among these digits: $O=3$, $L=7$ (no carry), or $O=7$, $L=1$ (carry $1$, since $4+7=11$).

- $O=3$, $L=7$: the tens column needs $I+6=9$, i.e. $I=3=O$, impossible.
- $O=7$, $L=1$ with a carry: $1+I+6=9$ gives $I=2$; then $W=8$, $D=3$ since $8+5=13$.

Check: $824+59567=60391$. So $M+E+D+A+L=6+0+3+9+1=19$.

**Answer: 19**
